title: Sandwich Board Night
shortDescription: Deli-style sandwich board with meats, cheeses, and spreads for ten
subtitle: Deli-style sandwich board with meats, cheeses, and spreads for ten
description: A long sandwich board offers sliced turkey, ham, roast beef, three cheeses, and spreads with sub rolls and condiments. Crew assembles foot-long style sandwiches or half subs depending on appetite.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Sandwich Board Night in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use mayonnaise as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch mixed. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Slice and arrange proteins
steps.instruction: Fan sliced turkey, ham, and roast beef in separate rows on the board or in hotel pans. Fold rather than stack flat so slices lift easily without tearing. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Prep cheeses and produce
steps.instruction: Arrange provolone, cheddar, and Swiss alongside meats. Set lettuce, tomato, and onion in produce pans with tongs for easy grabbing.

steps.title: Warm the rolls
steps.instruction: Split sub rolls and warm cut-side up at 325°F for 5–6 minutes until soft inside and lightly crisp at the edges. Wrap in towels until the board opens. Target oven/smoker temperature: 325°F.

steps.title: Set spreads and condiments
steps.instruction: Fill squeeze bottles and ramekins with mayo, mustard, oil-vinegar, pickles, and pepperoncini. Place salt and pepper grinders at the end of the line.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Sandwich Board Night onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Open the sandwich board
steps.instruction: Call crew to build sandwiches assembly-line style. Offer to press built subs on a griddle for crews wanting melted cheese without extra cook time.

proTips: A drizzle of red wine vinegar on the board keeps deli flavors bright and authentic.
Pre-toast one side of each roll for structural integrity on saucy builds.
Leftover sliced meats freeze well for the next sandwich board night.
tonightSpread: Full deli board with three meats, three cheeses, and warm sub rolls.
Chips and pickles for classic sub shop completeness.
leftovers: Chop meats and cheese into a breakfast scramble with peppers.
Layer into pressed panini the next day with leftover spreads.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Sandwich board night requires zero cooking during service if prep is done right. It works after training nights, during paperwork evenings, or whenever the oven is occupied elsewhere.
mealPrepNotes: Slice all meats and cheeses the night before on a deli slicer or with a sharp knife. Store in separate containers with parchment between layers. Rolls can be warmed in the oven just before service.
